title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: include or exclude default file path exclusions on Windows
summary: Hold: Microsoft has not documented that excluding the managed list restores monitoring of system paths, so the briefing gives administrators an assurance they cannot yet rely on. The existing configuration path, PowerShell call, licensing and roadmap dates are supported, but coexistence with manual exclusions and an unchanged identity model are also asserted beyond the available evidence.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans an Endpoint DLP control to include or exclude default Windows file path exclusions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention: Add control to include or exclude Default file paths exclusions for Windows

claims.claim: The roadmap says customers previously configured system-file inclusions or exclusions manually.
claims.quote: Previously customers would have system files either included or excluded manually configured.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes providing the list by default with an option to include or exclude those paths.
claims.quote: With this feature there is now a capability to provide this by default and have the option of including or excluding those paths.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: No UI control or automation to include or exclude the Microsoft-managed default Windows list is yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP Windows default file path exclusions Set-PolicyConfig EndpointDlpGlobalSettings Microsoft Graph API recommended exclusions. Read Configure endpoint DLP settings and Set-PolicyConfig: manual PathExclusion and a Mac toggle, no managed Windows switch.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published the contents or display mechanism of the new managed Windows list; Learn currently lists only two default Windows paths.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "default" "Windows" "Microsoft-managed". Read Configure endpoint DLP settings and roadmap; neither supplies the new list's contents or viewing method. The settings page lists two existing default Windows exclusions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap does not explain how the managed list changes over time, how changes are announced or how administrators view it.
claims.quote: With this feature there is now a capability to provide this by default and have the option of including or excluding those paths. This list is managed by Microsoft to ensure accuracy and ease of management.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no information about the performance effect of excluding the list.
claims.quote: Previously customers would have system files either included or excluded manually configured. With this feature there is now a capability to provide this by default and have the option of including or excluding those paths.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a path-exclusion control without describing new data access or permissions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention: Add control to include or exclude Default file paths exclusions for Windows

claims.claim: No autonomous actions are described in the roadmap.
claims.quote: This list is managed by Microsoft to ensure accuracy and ease of management.

claims.claim: The new control makes no change to identity or access.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "file path exclusions" "identity" "permissions". Read roadmap and Configure endpoint DLP settings. Neither describes the new control's identity or access implications; a roadmap that mentions no such change does not establish that none occurs.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: "The roadmap describes a path-exclusion setting and does not describe new data access or permissions."

claims.claim: Administrator-entered Windows exclusions and the Microsoft-managed default list will coexist as two layers.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "exclusions" "coexist" "default". Read Configure endpoint DLP settings and roadmap. They document existing manual exclusions and a planned managed list separately, but do not describe coexistence or their interaction.
claims.fix: Replace "Two layers of exclusion will coexist: paths administrators add themselves under File path exclusions for Windows, and the Microsoft-managed default list. When a file is not audited, check both before raising a support case." with "Confirm how the Microsoft-managed default list interacts with administrator-entered Windows path exclusions before using it to troubleshoot missing audit activity."

claims.claim: Excluding the managed list leaves system paths subject to DLP monitoring.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "exclude" "default" "system paths" monitoring. Read roadmap and Configure endpoint DLP settings. No passage establishes restored monitoring from this new control, or how it interacts with manual and existing default exclusions.
claims.fix: Replace "Excluding the list leaves system paths subject to DLP monitoring." with "Confirm whether excluding the Microsoft-managed list restores monitoring for the system paths you need to cover."

claims.claim: Activity explorer can be used to review audit activity from onboarded devices.
claims.quote: Once a device is onboarded, it should be visible in the devices list, and should start reporting audit activity to Activity explorer.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published role requirements specifically for changing the new managed Windows exclusions control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP settings" "permissions" "role". Read Purview permissions and Configure endpoint DLP settings, and searched for the managed Windows exclusions control; no role requirement for that specific new control was found.
